name: huexpress
why: A PC Engine emulator; running retro hardware software opens a door into old console internals.

brief.what_it_is: HuExpress is a multi-platform emulator for the PC Engine, also known as the TurboGrafx-16. You give it a game file (the README lists ROM, ISO, ISQ, ZIP, and HCD formats), an optional backup RAM file, and options, and it runs the game in a window with OpenGL video and SDL sound. It is a fork of the Hu-Go! emulator by zeograd. The README is dated version 3.0.4, November 25th, 2017, and calls itself a first release with bugs expected. The Homebrew formula installs two executables, huexpress and hucrc.
brief.why_it_exists: The author forked Hu-Go! because it seemed abandoned, with no updates since 2005, and its BeOS support had been slowly breaking since version 2.10.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the emulator is based on a PC Engine emulator by Bero, with improvements from Hmmx's homepage, and that it reads its settings from huexpress.ini first and then from the command line. Developers can read and change many internal game variables through shared memory (identifier 25679), and can pause or step the CPU through the s_external_control_cpu field. The built-in cheat tool works by searching RAM for a value you type in while the game is paused (F1), then freezing or setting it (F2 and F3).

commands_seen.context: Basic usage line from the README. ROM is the game file, BACKUPMEM is the backup RAM file, and OPTION is a flag such as -c, -f, -m, -u, or -w. The ROM name must come before the backup RAM name.
From the INSTALL file, run after installing the dependencies to build HuExpress from source on Linux. The file says there is no automated installation step.

brief.install_notes: The README says installation is covered in the INSTALL file. Building from source on Linux needs gcc or clang, scons, and the libzip, SDL2, SDL2_mixer, and libvorbis development packages, then running scons. Haiku needs scons, gcc 4 or gcc_x86, and the gcc4 SDL2, SDL2_mixer, libzip, and libvorbis packages. Windows needs MinGW, MSYS, and the SDL development libraries for MinGW. On FreeBSD the sdl-config script is named sdl2-config, so you need to link it. Settings go in huexpress.ini, where the variables include rom_dir, snd_freq, buffer_size, cd_path, and window_size. For CD games on Linux, set cd_path (default /dev/cdrom). For CD games on any platform, you need a system card ROM, usually called syscard.pce, which the README says you can only use if you own the original hardware or hucard.
brief.standout: It is a small, readable C codebase that is honest about its state and keeps the Hu-Go! heritage in the open. The README also has a full cheat-search workflow, including relative searches such as +1 or -1, and an exposed shared-memory interface for tools that want to inspect or drive the CPU.
brief.status: quiet. The README's most recent dated entry is version 3.0.4 from November 25th, 2017. I did not see a newer release, and the fetched pages did not show a last commit date, so I cannot tell whether development has continued since then.
brief.caveats: Platforms in the README are Linux, Haiku, Mac OS X (homebrew), and FreeBSD, which is marked untested. The FAQ says Windows is not supported, although the INSTALL file has MinGW notes. The FAQ on Mac OS X is contradictory: it says patches are welcome for an SDL version, which suggests the Homebrew route may be less settled than the requirements list implies. Known issues listed in the README are that fullscreen is broken and does not scale, netplay is not functional, and game state save is known to crash. The README also says the FreeBSD CD support does not exist yet, and the cheat tool has no visual help. The disclaimer says the software comes with no warranty and that the developer does not condone piracy. The HCD format documentation is in a doc/ folder that I did not open.
quotes: This is the first release of HuExpress, a multi-platform PC Engine emulator.
Bugs are expected as this is all new code.
Please only use HuExpress to play PC Engine games and backups you legally own.
